title: Classroom & Study Objects
description: Build essential vocabulary for study tools and master simple prepositions of place.
objectives: Identify common stationery and classroom equipment by name
Ask and answer 'What is this/that?' and 'What are these/those?' fluently
Describe object locations using basic prepositions (on, in, under, next to)

vocabularyList.definition: An instrument for writing or drawing, consisting of a thin stick of graphite.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: You can write your notes with a pencil.

vocabularyList.definition: An instrument for writing or drawing with ink.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Sign the registration form with a blue pen.

vocabularyList.definition: A book of blank or ruled pages for writing notes.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Keep your grammar notes in this notebook.

vocabularyList.definition: A piece of rubber used for rubbing out pencil marks.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Use an eraser if you make a mistake.

vocabularyList.definition: A straight strip used to measure distance or draw straight lines.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Draw a straight line with your ruler.

vocabularyList.definition: A piece of furniture with a flat surface used for working or studying.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Every student has their own desk in class.

vocabularyList.definition: A smooth white surface for writing on with dry-wipe markers.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: The teacher wrote the new words on the whiteboard.

vocabularyList.definition: A bag carried on one's back with two straps.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Put your books inside your backpack.

vocabularyList.definition: A felt-tipped pen used for bold writing or drawing.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: We need a black marker for the whiteboard.

vocabularyList.definition: A reference book listing words and their meanings.
vocabularyList.exampleSentence: Look up unfamiliar vocabulary in the dictionary.

sections.title: Study Objects & Locational Phrases
sections.content:
To describe your study environment, pair object names with **prepositions of place**:
- **on**: resting on top of a surface (*on the desk*)
- **in**: located inside a container (*in the backpack*)
- **under**: below something (*under the chair*)
- **next to**: by the side of (*next to the computer*)

callouts.title: Question Contractions
callouts.text: Native speakers often say **What's this?** and **Where's the pen?** in everyday speech.

callouts.title: Preposition Accuracy
callouts.text: Say **on the desk** (surface), not **in the desk** (unless it is inside a drawer).

sections.title: Lesson Summary
summaryPoints: Master common study items: pen, pencil, notebook, eraser, ruler, whiteboard, backpack.
Use 'on' for flat surfaces (on the desk, on the whiteboard).
Use 'in' for containers (in the bag, in the pencil case).
Use 'under' for below an object (under the chair).
Ask 'What is this/that?' for singular items and 'What are these/those?' for plurals.
